name: Gulf / US–Iran war
summary: Qatari mediators met Iranian officials on 20–21 Nov; Iran calls the US blockade an act of war; no ceasefire or deal
state: A Qatari delegation held talks in Tehran on 20 Nov, and Deputy Foreign Minister Gharibabadi said on 21 Nov the contacts are not yet formal negotiations and called the US blockade of Iranian ports an act of war (Al Jazeera). US envoys Witkoff and Kushner met Qatari mediators on 20 Nov (Axios). Lloyd's List Intelligence counted 550 non-Iranian Hormuz transits in October, the most since the war began, but seven attacks on ships on 5–11 Nov. Attacks on shipping and no ceasefire keep the Alert.
for_you: Shipping, fuel and freight costs remain exposed to attacks around Hormuz. Travellers to the Gulf should follow FCDO travel advice, which can change at short notice.
rubric_hit: Attacks on Gulf shipping continue with no ceasefire = Alert

why: Direct hostilities between Iran and the US or Israel threaten Gulf energy infrastructure, the Strait of Hormuz and the wider region.
drivers: Strikes and retaliation, attacks on shipping and Gulf states, mediation and ceasefire talks, US force posture.

rubric.alert: Active strikes between states, attacks on Gulf energy infrastructure or shipping, or the Strait of Hormuz substantially closed.
rubric.watch: A ceasefire or stalemate with sporadic strikes, or credible threats of renewed strikes.
rubric.normal: No direct state-on-state hostilities; diplomacy active.
